# Traceability Report

`mxcli report traceability` is the requirements-side counterpart of the tests report:
the tests report asks "what do the tests reach?", this one asks "is each requirement
built and proven?". Nothing on it is ticked off by hand.

## Preconditions

1. **Requirements are in the brain.** The report refuses to run without
   `docs/brain/plan/`. A PRD item nobody captured cannot appear — capture each one,
   anchored where it will be built, with its place in the spec at the end of the
   title:

   ```bash
   mxcli brain capture "Colleagues can offer a shift (slide 7)" --slice 02-swaps \
     -a @Swaps.ACT_OfferShift -p app.mpr
   ```

2. **Anchor where it is built**, not where it is talked about: the microflow, page,
   entity, attribute or published service that implements it. A role, enumeration or
   constant anchor has no microflow footprint; the page says "no microflow implements
   this", not "untested".
3. **Verdicts live on decisions.** When the build differs from the spec, record it
   on the decision, in its body, so `brain check` can validate the id:

   ```text
   Changes requirement `a1b2c3`: approval is per team, not per person.
   Partly meets requirement `d4e5f6`: web only; mobile in M3.
   ```

4. **Milestones** map slices (and single requirements) to the spec's milestones in
   `docs/brain/plan/traceability.json`:

   ```json
   {"milestones": [
     {"name": "M1 — accounts", "slices": ["01-accounts"]},
     {"name": "M2 — swaps", "slices": ["02-swaps"], "requirements": ["a1b2c3"]}
   ]}
   ```

## Run it

```bash
mxcli report traceability -p app.mpr --junit results.xml \
  --journeys journeys.jsonl --spans spans.jsonl -o docs/traceability.html
```

Evidence flags are the tests report's (`--tests`, `--junit`, `--run`, `--journeys`,
`--spans`, `--journeys-cmd`); see `report-tests` for their preconditions (fresh
seed, tracing on, never commit while tests run).

## Reading it

- **Status** — `built`: every anchor resolves (the same check as `brain plan`; the
  command refuses to report if the two disagree). `partial` / `changed`: a decision
  says so. `not built`: an anchor does not resolve. `not traceable`: no anchors.
- **Implemented by** is the footprint: the anchored microflow and its same-module
  callees, microflows a page/workflow/service calls, microflows that write an anchored
  entity, use an anchored attribute or association. Helpers with more than three
  callers are left out — they belong to no single requirement.
- **Tests / journeys** reach the footprint (or the journey log names an anchored
  page — needed for pages with only database data sources, which run no microflow).
- **Decisions / open questions** share an anchor or cite the id. Linking by shared
  anchor is noisy around hub elements; cite the id in the body when it matters.

The three gap lists at the bottom are the work queue: not built as asked, built but
untested, and open questions that affect a requirement. Answer questions with
`mxcli brain resolve`; the next run moves them.

## Related

- `report-tests` — the same evidence per module instead of per requirement.
